title: Sylow theorems as a partial converse to Lagrange

problemStatement.formal: State and prove Lagrange divisibility, Sylow existence/cardinality/conjugacy/counting, prime-power subgroup existence, and Cauchy's theorem for finite groups.
problemStatement.plain: Formalize the Sylow theorems as the prime-power partial converse to Lagrange's theorem, together with Cauchy's theorem.
whyMatters: Sylow theory is the main positive answer left after the full converse to Lagrange fails for composite divisors.
The proof packages standard Mathlib finite group theory into a gallery-ready entry.

proven: lagrange, lagrange_index, and order_dvd_card provide the Lagrange layer.
sylow_exists, sylow_card_eq, sylow_conjugate, sylow_count_dvd_index, and sylow_count_mod_p package the three Sylow theorems.
